scope: Remove repeated grid interpolation and parameter interpretation that limit playback Worker frame supply; preserve the exact rendering result and measure actual model-update FPS against the frozen task-start build.

outcome.interpretation: The final combined change increases mean displayed model-update FPS by 4.71% and median FPS by 3.32%. All four predetermined adjacent pairs improve by 2.53% to 7.06%. This is a local-model result, not a universal speedup or a claim of sustained 120FPS. The frozen original measured about 108FPS in this final series; the earlier 80s FPS figures were from separate system conditions and are not used as the denominator.

environment.renderer: WebGL; Metal backend enforced and verified by pixel comparisons
environment.gpuAvailability: User reported the competing GPU job had finished. Other applications were not stopped. No test/build/profile work from this task ran concurrently with the final FPS series.

diagnosis.cause: Worker frame supply, including repeated interpolation and numeric parameter resolution, limits fresh frames despite available browser rAF callbacks. The trace did not show ready frames waiting for their target time or a meaningful delay before issuing another Worker request.

sharedGridShapes.evidence: Temporary prototype console count in compute-shared-grids-full.log; no production counters.

diagnosis.timingLimits: Diagnostic Date.now timers have 1ms granularity and include scheduling/descheduling. The first diagnostic also sampled CPU profiles. These locate work/waits and are separate from uninstrumented throughput/FPS measurements.

changes.change: Prepare and share axes, keyform-index layout and the latest continuous/discrete interpolation points for equivalent immutable bindings. Identity includes parameter order, keyform order and sampling policy, with distinct signed-zero/nonfinite keys. Channel/rest coordinates and repeat-range/value guards remain independent.

Compile parameter lookups and share the latest readonly resolved tuple for the same document/axes. Compare raw scalar inputs with Object.is and allocate a new tuple on change so prior snapshots remain unchanged. Only axes declared by the model are retained in the strong pool; ad hoc bindings use the weak index.
Prepare shared interpolation metadata once when the compute engine is created.

measurement.fpsMethod: A single visible Chrome player/canvas per run; create/destroy a fresh page/player for each artifact. Orders ABBA and BAAB, 10 seconds warmup and 20 seconds measurement, four runs per artifact. No profiling or diagnostic instrumentation; retain every run.
measurement.modelFPSDefinition: Count browser rAF intervals in which the player onFrame publication counter changes, divided by elapsed rAF time. This measures fresh model updates rather than browser callbacks or Worker request count; physical panel scanout is not sampled.
measurement.frameP95Definition: Raw frameP95 is the browser rAF interval percentile, not the model-update interval percentile.
measurement.numericMethod: One Chrome, both numeric Workers initialized, only one advanced at a time. Fixed 1/60 simulation delta, 1200 warmup frames per variant, ABBA three times, 300 full round trips per window, six windows per artifact. No GPU drawing. This is a Worker roundtrip benchmark, not actual playback FPS.
